# Thread Status

Use the live Codex thread tools to review recent threads and update their titles. Do not rely on local session-index files unless the live thread tools are unavailable and the user explicitly accepts local-only coverage.

## Workflow

1. List up to 30 recent threads across available hosts. Respect a different limit or scope supplied by the user.
2. Exclude automation-run threads. Treat threads as peers even when one created, delegated to, or coordinates another.
3. Read the latest completed turn of each candidate with outputs disabled. Read one additional turn only when the thread's own pending responsibility is unclear.
4. Classify the thread using only its own contract:
   - `✅` — Its requested result was delivered or completion was clearly reported, with no pending work or retained responsibility.
   - `🚨` — It explicitly awaits user input, approval, credentials, permission, a choice, or another action only the user can provide.
   - `⏳` — Its work remains active, monitored, pending on tools or remote work, or genuinely uncertain.
5. Be conservative with `✅`. Idle UI state is not proof of completion. An error is not `🚨` when the thread is still handling it autonomously. Standing monitors and recurring work remain `⏳` unless explicitly paused or ended.
6. Classify coordinators independently:
   - Mark a parent `✅` when it finished dispatching, steering, or reporting and retained no monitoring or follow-up responsibility, even if a child remains `⏳`.
   - Mark a parent `⏳` only when the parent itself retains coordination, monitoring, or follow-up work.
   - Mark a parent `🚨` only when the parent's own next step awaits the user.
7. Build the title:
   - Use exactly one status prefix and one space.
   - Strip any existing `✅`, `🚨`, or `⏳` prefix first.
   - Preserve a useful title body when the topic is unchanged.
   - Otherwise use a concise title body describing the thread's current task.
   - If only status changed, change only the prefix.
8. Rename only when the resulting title differs. Do not message, archive, pin, fork, or otherwise alter threads.
9. Handle the calling thread last. If this status pass completes its only requested work, mark it `✅` immediately before the final response; otherwise classify its remaining responsibility normally.
10. Report changed titles and genuine uncertainties concisely. If nothing changed, say so.

# Thread Status

Use the live Codex thread tools to review recent threads and update their titles. Do not rely on local session-index files unless the live thread tools are unavailable and the user explicitly accepts local-only coverage.

## Workflow

1. List up to 30 recent threads across available hosts. Respect a different limit or scope supplied by the user.
2. Exclude automation-run threads. Treat threads as peers even when one created, delegated to, or coordinates another.
3. Read the latest completed turn of each candidate with outputs disabled. Read one additional turn only when the thread's own pending responsibility is unclear.
4. Classify the thread using only its own contract:
   - `✅` — Its requested result was delivered or completion was clearly reported, with no pending work or retained responsibility.
   - `🚨` — It explicitly awaits user input, approval, credentials, permission, a choice, or another action only the user can provide.
   - `⏳` — Its work remains active, monitored, pending on tools or remote work, or genuinely uncertain.
5. Be conservative with `✅`. Idle UI state is not proof of completion. An error is not `🚨` when the thread is still handling it autonomously. Standing monitors and recurring work remain `⏳` unless explicitly paused or ended.
6. Classify coordinators independently:
   - Mark a parent `✅` when it finished dispatching, steering, or reporting and retained no monitoring or follow-up responsibility, even if a child remains `⏳`.

   - Mark a parent `🚨` only when the parent's own next step awaits the user.
7. Build the title:
   - Use exactly one status prefix and one space.
   - Strip any existing `✅`, `🚨`, or `⏳` prefix first.
   - Preserve a useful title body when the topic is unchanged.
   - Otherwise use a concise title body describing the thread's current task.

+# Docs deployment tooling
+
+This directory owns repository-side validation, workflow receipt checks,
+provider/state inventory and report-only orphan classification for the docs
+application. Durable resource and proof policy lives in

+- `schemas.ts`, `workflow-receipts.schemas.ts`,
+  `workflow-check.schemas.ts`, `inventory.schemas.ts`, and
+  `orphan-inventory.schemas.ts` own external representations and closed safe
+  errors.

+  ingress through Effect FileSystem, Crypto and Schema.

+  shared boundary and one typed verification program, logs safe fields through
+  Effect Console, provides Bun services and executes through
+  `BunRuntime.runMain`.
+- `inventory.runtime.ts` and `orphan-inventory.runtime.ts` are executable
+  composition owners. Their services remain report-only unless a separately
+  authorized workflow owns mutation.
+- `alchemy.run.ts` remains the root Alchemy resource composition; this tool
+  directory does not own the Worker graph.
+
+The workflow adapters do not read `process.env`, use `Bun.file`, parse JSON
+manually, orchestrate raw Promises, call `Effect.runPromise`, write through
+`console`, or set process exit state. Config and receipt values decode once at
+ingress and internal failures remain tagged as input, read or mismatch errors.
+Logs and receipts contain safe identity only, never credential values or raw
+provider payloads.
+
+## Local verification
+
+```sh
+bun run check:docs-deployment:types
+bun run check:docs-deployment-tools:types
+bun run test:docs-deployment
+bun run check:docs-deployment
+```
+
+The tests include adversarial Config/receipt fixtures and static adapter
+contracts. The retained-evidence check validates historical claim matching.
+These local commands do not dispatch workflows, access providers, deploy,
+destroy, prove hosted behavior or grant operational authority.

Yes—mainly repository tooling, deployment verification, and internal runtime architecture.

What changed functionally:

- Deployment/checking scripts now handle configuration, credentials, files, JSON, child processes and errors through strict Effect boundaries.
- The docs app’s server runtime now manages its diagnostic identity/state through Effect instead of global randomness and mutable variables.
- The built-app verification gained stronger server-function, runtime-reuse and screenshot proof.

What did not change:

- Tax calculations, rules, SDK and API functionality.
- Public documentation content or navigation.
- The visible docs-site design or intended browser behaviour.
- The Alchemy/Cloudflare resource graph.
- Preview, Production, domains, DNS or deployed resources.
- Package versions or public exports.

So the docs app’s real production server path was improved, but the change was deliberately behaviour-preserving. Users should see the same site; maintainers now get safer runtime internals and much stronger evidence that it works correctly.

What is the purpose of this?
"The docs app’s server runtime now manages its diagnostic identity/state through Effect instead of global randomness and mutable variables." and "
2. Workflow file and receipt handling gained a shared boundary"

Both are foundation/verification improvements, not new customer-facing features.

1. **Effect-managed diagnostic identity/state**

The docs server emits diagnostics that help prove whether requests are being handled by the same running server instance. Previously, that proof relied on a global mutable counter and direct random UUID generation.

Now Effect owns:

- The server instance ID.
- The changing diagnostic state.
- Randomness and state updates.
- Deterministic replacements during tests.

Purpose: avoid race-prone global variables, make lifecycle behaviour explicit, and let tests reliably prove that the server runtime survives across multiple requests. It does **not** change normal page content or functionality.

2. **Shared workflow file and receipt boundary**

A “receipt” here is an evidence file produced or checked by deployment workflows—for example, identifying the commit, artifact, or verification result associated with a deployment.

Previously, several scripts independently read files, parsed JSON, and calculated hashes. The shared boundary now centralises:

- File access.
- JSON validation.
- SHA-256 calculation.
- Typed failure handling.
- Test substitutes.

Purpose: ensure every deployment-verification script interprets evidence consistently and fails safely when a receipt is missing, malformed, or does not match the expected artifact/commit. This mainly improves CI and deployment assurance—not TaxKit calculations or the visible docs experience.

I’ll inspect the exact implementation and installed Effect v4 APIs before answering whether these helpers are justified or should be replaced. I’m using the strict Effect guidance because this is specifically an Effect architecture review.

The code already uses Effect Platform’s child-process APIs for spawning. I’m checking whether `@effect/cli` is installed or relevant here, and whether these two helpers add semantic policy beyond what `Command` itself supplies.

Yes—but the code is already using the native Effect v4 process API. The two helpers add TaxKit-specific security and decoding policy that Effect’s generic process API cannot know.

1. `makeDocsDeploymentChildEnvironment`

This builds the exact environment given to each child command.

- The Alchemy/Cloudflare command receives only its required credentials.
- The GitHub command receives only `GH_TOKEN`.
- `extendEnv: false` prevents unrelated ambient secrets—npm, AWS, other Cloudflare tokens, etc.—from leaking into either process.

That is an important security boundary. `ChildProcess.make` accepts an environment, but it does not decide which credentials each TaxKit operation should be allowed to see.

2. `restoreDocsDeploymentJsonCommand(...)`

This turns raw command results back into a trusted TaxKit value:

1. Decode stdout and stderr as strict UTF-8.
2. Check the exit code.
3. Convert failures into closed, secret-safe tagged errors.
4. Decode successful stdout using the supplied Schema.
5. Reject malformed JSON and unexpected properties.

Effect’s process package gives us bytes, streams, and an exit code. It cannot know that stdout must be a particular TaxKit deployment Schema or which error details are safe to retain.

That said, I think this API is slightly over-shaped:

```ts
restoreDocsDeploymentJsonCommand(
  operation,
  exitCode,
  stdout,
  stderr,
  schema
)
```

A clearer name and parameter object would be better:

```ts
decodeDocsDeploymentCommandResult({
  operation,
  exitCode,
  stdout,
  stderr,
  schema,
})
```

Or the spawning, collection and decoding could become one named semantic operation such as `readDeploymentInventory`. The current split mainly exists to test the decoder without launching real processes.

On native Effect packages: TaxKit is pinned to Effect `4.0.0-beta.100`. In that version:

- OS commands are under `effect/unstable/process`.
- CLI argument parsing is under `effect/unstable/cli`.
- `@effect/cli` and the older `@effect/platform/Command` arrangement are not the applicable APIs.

The implementation already uses:

```ts
import {
  ChildProcess,
  ChildProcessSpawner,
} from "effect/unstable/process";
```

The Effect CLI module is unnecessary here because `check:docs-deployment-orphans` is a fixed, no-argument verification executable whose inputs come from typed `Config`. It would become appropriate if this evolved into a human-facing CLI with subcommands such as `inventory`, `plan`, or `apply`.

So my assessment is:

- Keep the explicit environment policy.
- Keep Schema-based command-result decoding.
- Continue using the current native Effect v4 process API.
- Don’t add Effect CLI merely for ceremony.
- Consider renaming/consolidating the five-argument restoration helper because its current shape makes the call graph look more complicated than the underlying responsibility really is.

That concern is reasonable. I’m tracing what the spawned processes actually do, then comparing it with the installed Alchemy version and its official development/deployment model. I’m using the Alchemy IaC guidance because this is an infrastructure-boundary question, not merely a TypeScript style question.

The spawned commands are not running the docs development server or performing deployment. Yes—your instinct is mostly right. Two separate things have become conflated.

The child spawning is only used by the report-only orphan-preview audit. It:

1. Spawns TaxKit’s own `bun run check:docs-deployment-inventory`.
2. Spawns `gh pr list`.
3. Combines Alchemy/Cloudflare resources with open GitHub PRs to identify abandoned preview environments.

It does not build, serve or deploy the docs app.

The security intention was sensible—give each subprocess only its permitted credentials—but spawning our own inventory command and then reparsing its stdout is unnecessarily indirect. The same Effect service can be composed directly in the orphan-inventory runtime. GitHub PRs could likewise come through a small typed GitHub HTTP service rather than `gh`.

Alchemy does not recommend subprocess orchestration as its application-development model.

For TanStack Start, current Alchemy guidance is:

- Declare the application as `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`.
- Let Alchemy add its Cloudflare Vite integration.
- Remove the separate `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`.
- Use `alchemy dev` for integrated Vite/HMR development.
- Use `alchemy deploy` for reconciliation and deployment.

That recommendation is present in both current Alchemy documentation and the installed `alchemy@2.0.0-beta.64`. [Alchemy’s TanStack Start guide](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/tanstack-start/) explicitly describes this setup.

TaxKit currently uses the older/manual composition:

```ts
Command.Build("DocsBuild", ...)
Cloudflare.Worker("DocsWebsite", ...)
```

in [alchemy.run.ts](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/alchemy.run.ts:1), while [vite.config.ts](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/docs/vite.config.ts:1) directly installs the Cloudflare plugin. Alchemy’s current Vite resource is designed to replace that manual build-plus-worker assembly. [Alchemy’s Vite documentation](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite/) describes it as one resource owning the Vite build, SSR Worker and assets.

My recommended correction is:

- Replace `Command.Build + Cloudflare.Worker` with `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`.
- Remove the manually configured Cloudflare Vite plugin.
- Keep ordinary Vite development if we value a very fast infrastructure-free loop.
- Add `alchemy dev` as the authoritative Cloudflare-integrated development path.
- Stop spawning TaxKit’s inventory executable from the orphan audit; compose its service directly.
- Replace `gh pr list` with a typed GitHub API adapter if the orphan audit remains valuable.
- Delete `makeDocsDeploymentChildEnvironment` and `restoreDocsDeploymentJsonCommand` once no subprocess boundary remains.

One important distinction: `alchemy dev` is not the replacement for orphan detection. It continuously plans/applies the stack and runs the development server, whereas orphan detection must remain read-only. [Alchemy’s lifecycle documentation](https://v2.alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource-lifecycle/) confirms that `alchemy dev` runs the lifecycle continuously.

So the short verdict is: the credential isolation goal was good, but the subprocess architecture overcompensated. The docs app should move toward native `Website.Vite`/`alchemy dev`, while the orphan audit should become a straightforward in-process Effect composition.

+This directory owns repository-side validation, workflow receipt checks and

+operator procedure and authority live in

+
+## Current boundaries
+
+- `schemas.ts`, `workflow-receipts.schemas.ts`, `workflow-check.schemas.ts` and
+  `inventory.schemas.ts` own current external representations and closed safe
+  errors. `schemas.ts` also decodes immutable two-resource v1 receipts while

+  state construction.

+  shared boundary and one typed verification program, logs safe fields through
+  Effect Console, provides Bun services and executes once through

+  remains read-only unless a separately authorized workflow owns mutation.

+  adapters for ambient host access, raw concurrency, lost workflow/credential
+  boundaries and unmanaged docs runtime state.

+`runPromise`. This is a framework adapter, not domain execution ownership.

+```sh
+bun run check:docs-deployment:types
+bun run check:docs-deployment-tools:types
+bun run test:docs-deployment
+bun run check:docs-deployment

+historical receipt classification and static adapter contracts. Root
+`verification` invokes them once. These local commands do not dispatch
+workflows, access providers, deploy, destroy, prove hosted behavior or grant
+operational authority.

+

content.text: The audit is complete in substance. I’m pulling its final findings now so I can separate real fixes from historical or optional improvements.

Yes. The core Alchemy setup is correct: one native `Cloudflare.Website.Vite` resource, with no unnecessary child process.

The audit found five real improvements:

1. **Production runs can cancel active deployments**  
   `.github/workflows/docs-production.yml` uses `cancel-in-progress: true` for the same lock as deploy and rollback. This should be changed so an active production mutation cannot be cancelled.

2. **Cloudflare credentials are exposed too broadly**  
   The token is currently available to the whole Preview and Production jobs, including build and third-party steps. It should only be attached to the exact provider-operation steps.

3. **Alchemy bootstrap is more powerful than documented**  
   Alchemy beta.64 can refresh credentials, upload a temporary Worker, and create or upgrade its state store. Our docs currently describe this as simple cache preparation. The wording and receipts need correcting.

4. **Hosted-proof inputs are not fully validated**  
   Some environment values are read as raw strings and parsed with `parseInt`, so malformed input such as `12junk` could be accepted. These inputs should use Effect Config and Schema.

5. **The deployment runbook is stale**  
   It still contains old `DocsBuild` plus `DocsWebsite` instructions, even though the current design only uses `DocsWebsite`. The old material should be clearly marked historical and the current procedure made authoritative.

There are also three smaller recommendations:

- Move repeated workflow shell logic into one typed Effect command.
- Add real sanitised Alchemy plan fixtures to tests.
- Document that GitHub workflow locks do not necessarily protect against manual Alchemy CLI runs.

No files, credentials, deployments, or provider resources were changed by the audit.

---

# Thread Status

Use the live Codex thread tools to review recent threads and update their titles. Do not rely on local session-index files unless the live thread tools are unavailable and the user explicitly accepts local-only coverage.

## Workflow

1. List up to 30 recent threads across available hosts. Respect a different limit or scope supplied by the user.
2. Exclude automation-run threads. Treat threads as peers even when one created, delegated to, or coordinates another.
3. Read the latest completed turn of each candidate with outputs disabled. Read one additional turn only when the thread's own pending responsibility is unclear.
4. Classify the thread using only its own contract:
   - `✅` — Its requested result was delivered or completion was clearly reported, with no pending work or retained responsibility.
   - `🚨` — It explicitly awaits user input, approval, credentials, permission, a choice, or another action only the user can provide.
   - `⏳` — Its work remains active, monitored, pending on tools or remote work, or genuinely uncertain.
5. Be conservative with `✅`. Idle UI state is not proof of completion. An error is not `🚨` when the thread is still handling it autonomously. Standing monitors and recurring work remain `⏳` unless explicitly paused or ended.
6. Classify coordinators independently:
   - Mark a parent `✅` when it finished dispatching, steering, or reporting and retained no monitoring or follow-up responsibility, even if a child remains `⏳`.
   - Mark a parent `⏳` only when the parent itself retains coordination, monitoring, or follow-up work.
   - Mark a parent `🚨` only when the parent's own next step awaits the user.
7. Build the title:
   - Use exactly one status prefix and one space.
   - Strip any existing `✅`, `🚨`, or `⏳` prefix first.
   - Preserve a useful title body when the topic is unchanged.
   - Otherwise use a concise title body describing the thread's current task.
   - If only status changed, change only the prefix.
8. Rename only when the resulting title differs. Do not message, archive, pin, fork, or otherwise alter threads.
9. Handle the calling thread last. If this status pass completes its only requested work, mark it `✅` immediately before the final response; otherwise classify its remaining responsibility normally.
10. Report changed titles and genuine uncertainties concisely. If nothing changed, say so.

name: prd-implementer
description: Implement an approved product or technical SPEC and its task list in small, verified, sequential slices. Use when executing repository plans that require Effect/TypeScript architecture, React composition, external SDK boundaries, documentation and README synchronization, lint and CI enforcement, repository-skill updates, or evidence-backed reconciliation of the SPEC and tasks as implementation discoveries arise.
---

# PRD Implementer

Implement the canonical SPEC as a sequence of accepted end-to-end slices. Keep code, documentation, enforcement, and planning artifacts synchronized.

## Start from current truth

1. Read applicable `AGENTS.md`, the exact SPEC, its sibling task list, active execution plan, relevant docs and READMEs, current worktree, installed dependency versions, package scripts, lint/test/CI configuration, and representative code.
2. Preserve unrelated changes. Confirm task dependencies and current completion evidence before editing.
3. Use DeepWiki through Executor MCP only for upstream libraries. Verify any guidance against the installed version and local types; never use DeepWiki as a substitute for reading the checkout.

Load context in layers: external systems own live external state, repository
docs own durable repository truth, and the active SPEC/tasks own the current
change. Pull current and affected owners just in time; link to history, raw
proof, and provider truth instead of copying them into the active context.

For substantial repository, operational, automation, migration, or harness
work, read the sibling
[`repository-harness-contract`](../docs-maintainer/references/repository-harness-contract.md)
once during grounding, including its contract map and invariant register. Apply
the stable invariant IDs through the owning task surfaces rather than copying
the references into the SPEC, code, or final report.

## Suggest one implementation goal

When an approved SPEC has multiple implementation tasks and no active goal,
suggest creating one goal for implementing the whole SPEC to verified
completion. Present the proposed objective in user-facing language and create
the goal only after the user explicitly requests or confirms it.

Use the SPEC's accepted tasks as sequential milestones inside that one goal;
do not create a separate goal for every task. Continue an existing matching
goal instead of replacing it. Keep the goal active until all accepted tasks,
documentation reconciliation, terminal review, and closeout verification are
complete. Goal state coordinates persistence across turns; it never replaces
the canonical task ledger, acceptance evidence, or proof receipts.

## Delegated Slice Prompt Contract

Keep one primary trajectory accountable for integration, proof, delivery, and
closeout. Delegate a bounded task only when it has an independently provable
boundary, benefits from fresh/adversarial evidence, or the task artifact proves
disjoint writes. Review delegated work and return an incomplete slice to the
same agent before acceptance. Do not use one-subagent-per-task or a fixed number
of audit passes as acceptance proof. Parallelize only when dependencies and
write scopes are explicitly disjoint.

Every delegated slice states the accepted outcome, exact target revision and
paths, applicable repository instructions, authority and stop conditions,
document/runbook/proof impact, commands or procedure owners, required receipt,
limitations, non-claims, and return-to-owner condition. The primary trajectory
reviews the evidence and owns merge, cross-surface reconciliation, rollback,
and task closure.

## Execute sequentially

For each task:

1. Re-state its owning paths, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and verification.
2. When work derives from an audit, confirm the task's accepted finding IDs.
   Validate the structured crosswalk when the repository provides its audit
   validator. Do not implement rejected, deferred, or optional findings without
   explicit acceptance.
3. For a material slice, load the sibling
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) and its local profile when
   present; establish the slice's documentation-impact rows.
4. Implement the smallest complete vertical slice.
5. Update the SPEC, tasks, diagrams, owning docs, necessary pointers, READMEs,
   lint/configuration, skills, and operational artifacts immediately when
   implementation evidence changes them.
6. Audit the diff for architecture, helper sprawl, boundary provenance, React composition, and enforcement.
7. Run the narrow proof first and broaden according to blast radius.
8. Record evidence and mark completion only when every required surface and
   documentation-impact row passes.

Do not preserve a fixed number of passes, subagents, files, or commands as a
process goal. Risk, dependencies, accepted outcomes, and evidence determine the
slice and verification depth.

## Effect implementation bar

- Use the repository's installed Effect APIs and established Service/Context and Layer style.
- Keep primary operations lazy, flat, readable, and sequential with `Effect.gen`, meaningful `Effect.fn`, or the local equivalent. Use combinators where they improve local composition.
- Keep one-use transformations and typed error handling inline. Extract only reused domain policy, independently testable behavior, or a real I/O boundary.
- Reuse canonical Schemas, schema-derived types, branded IDs, services, Layers, tagged errors, and constructors. Do not mirror DTOs or redeclare identifiers as raw strings.
- Decode unknown values once at the real boundary and encode values at outward transport boundaries.
- Use Schema-backed `Config`/`ConfigProvider` configuration and preserve redaction until immediate SDK construction.
- Keep expected failures typed; do not use `instanceof` for policy or provider-error classification.
- Keep Effects lazy until the repository's application/runtime boundary. Do not scatter `runPromise`, nested runtimes, ad hoc `try/catch`, or Promise islands.

For an external SDK, invoke the `effect-client-wrapper` contract. Reject generic `use` callbacks, exposed raw clients, raw `id: string`, primitive config, `instanceof`, and unchecked provider output. Require named operations, encoded requests, immediate output decoding, typed Schema errors, operation-specific retry policy, and live plus mock/test Layers.

## React implementation bar

- Compose data loading, shared state, and Effect execution at the route or feature boundary.
- Keep leaf components focused on rendering and local interaction through narrow readonly props and callbacks.
- Colocate one-use components; extract shared components or hooks only for demonstrated reuse or a stable semantic boundary.
- Cover semantic HTML, keyboard and focus behavior, loading, empty, error, disabled, and responsive states.
- Reject synchronization Effects, duplicated state, service-aware leaves, giant route components, boolean-prop matrices, and hooks that merely rename one call.

## Reconcile every surface

Before accepting a task, resolve every SPEC impact-ledger row for docs, READMEs, lint/custom rules and fixtures, CI, skills and agent instructions, configuration/manifests, Schemas/migrations/generators, tests/fixtures, observability, release, rollout, and rollback. A required surface cannot be deferred with a vague follow-up.

Use only commands that exist in the repository. Validate changed skills with the available skill validator. Distinguish pre-existing failures from regressions, and finish with changed paths, commands and outcomes, updated task status, and residual risks.

For material tasks, also reconcile the complete harness contract:

- respect truth layers and semantic owners; update the earliest durable owner
  and remove weaker duplicated reminders;
- keep skills as judgment/routing and runbooks as procedures with preconditions,
  authority, exact steps, bounded evidence, rollback, and escalation;
- emit bounded receipts with invariant, target, recovery, omitted-detail path,
  postcondition, artifact identity, limitations, and non-claims;
- match proof to the actual artifact, environment, boundary, and small
  consumer-visible critical journeys with an oracle against imitation;
- distinguish capability, authenticated identity, authority, and approval, and
  record revocation, duration, audit receipt, rollback, and escalation for
  consequential operations;
- admit automation only when signal, durable state, authority,
  idempotence/convergence, per-run proof, bounded failure, stopping, and
  escalation are settled;
- preserve the worker/host/tool/runtime/skill epoch and the four distinct
  clocks when evaluation claims depend on them; and
- retain failed, blocked, deferred, superseded, inconclusive, and no-op evidence
  with provenance, successor/tombstone, recovery, and explicit non-claims
  outside the default context route.

The docs-maintainer method and local profile own the local document map, exact
checks, archive and mirror rules, runbooks, and exceptions; this skill must not
invent them. Update owning docs and necessary pointers inside the
implementation slice. Mark every impact-ledger surface `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or `N/A` with evidence and attach its bounded receipt before task
acceptance.

## Close out the SPEC

Invoke docs-maintainer again before final task or SPEC closeout. Reconcile the
active SPEC, tasks, execution plan, lifecycle state, successor/tombstone and
archive pointers, proof packets, limitations, and non-claims against the
implemented repository. Run the exact local documentation and lifecycle checks
and mark completion only after current owners and planning artifacts agree.

For ordinary repository improvements, finish after the accepted important
corrections, normal repository checks, applicable real journeys, and one fresh
independent review. Preserve optional work as optional. Do not extend execution
into a comparative harness campaign unless that distinct claim and authority
were approved.

</skill>

# Thread Status

Use the live Codex thread tools to review recent threads and update their titles. Do not rely on local session-index files unless the live thread tools are unavailable and the user explicitly accepts local-only coverage.

## Workflow

1. List up to 30 recent threads across available hosts. Respect a different limit or scope supplied by the user.
2. Exclude automation-run threads. Treat threads as peers even when one created, delegated to, or coordinates another.
3. Read the latest completed turn of each candidate with outputs disabled. Read one additional turn only when the thread's own pending responsibility is unclear.
4. Classify the thread using only its own contract:
   - `✅` — Its requested result was delivered or completion was clearly reported, with no pending work or retained responsibility.
   - `🚨` — It explicitly awaits user input, approval, credentials, permission, a choice, or another action only the user can provide.
   - `⏳` — Its work remains active, monitored, pending on tools or remote work, or genuinely uncertain.
5. Be conservative with `✅`. Idle UI state is not proof of completion. An error is not `🚨` when the thread is still handling it autonomously. Standing monitors and recurring work remain `⏳` unless explicitly paused or ended.
6. Classify coordinators independently:
   - Mark a parent `✅` when it finished dispatching, steering, or reporting and retained no monitoring or follow-up responsibility, even if a child remains `⏳`.
   - Mark a parent `⏳` only when the parent itself retains coordination, monitoring, or follow-up work.
   - Mark a parent `🚨` only when the parent's own next step awaits the user.
7. Build the title:
   - Use exactly one status prefix and one space.
   - Strip any existing `✅`, `🚨`, or `⏳` prefix first.
   - Preserve a useful title body when the topic is unchanged.
   - Otherwise use a concise title body describing the thread's current task.
   - If only status changed, change only the prefix.
8. Rename only when the resulting title differs. Do not message, archive, pin, fork, or otherwise alter threads.
9. Handle the calling thread last. If this status pass completes its only requested work, mark it `✅` immediately before the final response; otherwise classify its remaining responsibility normally.
10. Report changed titles and genuine uncertainties concisely. If nothing changed, say so.

</skill>
